findings.title: IDOR: user can read another user's notifications
findings.description: get_notifications() takes the target user id from the request query params (`request.params.get("user_id", request.user_id)`) instead of always using the authenticated caller's id. Any authenticated user can pass a different `user_id` and read another user's notifications, which is an insecure direct object reference / broken access control vulnerability.

findings.title: IDOR: any user can mark any other user's notification as read
findings.description: post_notification_read() updates `notifications` by `id` alone, with no WHERE clause tying the row to `request.user_id`. Any authenticated caller can supply an arbitrary notification_id and mark (or tamper with the read state of) any other user's notifications.

findings.title: Weekly digest is marked read immediately after being sent
findings.description: After notify() inserts the new 'digest' notification for the user (line 92), send_weekly_digests() immediately runs `UPDATE notifications SET read_at = ? WHERE user_id = ?` with no filter excluding the just-created row. This sets read_at on the digest notification itself, so the user's inbox never actually contains an unread digest — the feature silently sends digests that are already 'read', defeating the purpose of the notification.

findings.title: Unvalidated notification_id can raise unhandled exception
findings.description: `int(request.body["notification_id"])` is not guarded; a non-numeric value in the request body will raise a ValueError that propagates as an unhandled server error (500) instead of a controlled 4xx response.

findings.title: Tautological assertion never fails
findings.description: `assert any(n["kind"] == "digest" for n in unread(db, user)) or True` always evaluates to True regardless of the `any(...)` result because of `or True`, so this assertion can never fail and provides no actual verification. Combined with the read-marking bug in send_weekly_digests, this test suite does not catch that the digest notification ends up already marked read and thus invisible in the unread list.
